pr.title: Disable jump threading `UnOp::Not` for non-bool
pr.description: Fix #131195, where jumpthreading was optimizing `!a == b` into `a != b` for non-bool, where this is definitely not true.
pr.author: compiler-errors

issues.title: `-Zmir-opt-level` miscompiles code with panic
issues.body:
<!--
Thank you for filing a bug report! 🐛 Please provide a short summary of the bug,
along with any information you feel relevant to replicating the bug.
-->

I tried this code:

```rust
pub fn myfunc() -> i32 {
    let mut c :i32 = 1;
    c = 1 ;
    if !c != 0 {
        return 1;
    }
    panic!("Reached end of non-void function");
}

pub fn main() {
    let e = myfunc();
    println!("e={}", e);
}
```

I expected to see this happen: **always panic**

Instead, this happened: **only -Zmir-opt-level=2 panic**

For mir-opt-level 0, 1 and 3, they all normally return
```shell
% rustc -Awarnings -Zmir-opt-level=2 test.rs && ./test
thread 'main' panicked at test.rs:7:5:
Reached end of non-void function
note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace
%
% rustc -Awarnings -Zmir-opt-level=0 test.rs && ./test
e=1
```

analysis.summary: JumpThreading's condition transfer for `Rvalue::UnaryOp(UnOp::Not, place)` inverted the polarity of the source condition as if `!` always acted as a logical not. That is valid only for `bool`; for integer operands `!` is a bitwise complement, so the pass wrongly treated `!a == b` (equivalently `(!a) == b`) as the negation of `a == b`, i.e. `a != b`. The fix guards the transfer with `place.ty(...).ty.is_bool()` and returns otherwise, leaving the condition unthreaded. The added MIR test records that `bitwise_not` keeps its `switchInt` rather than folding on the non-bool equality.
analysis.originalLogic: In `TOFinder`, when the copied RHS is `Rvalue::UnaryOp(UnOp::Not, Operand::Move(place) | Operand::Copy(place))`, the pass looks up the known conditions for `lhs` and the mapped `place`, then transfers `conditions.map(self.arena, Condition::inv)` to `place`. `Condition::inv` flips the polarity of the branch condition, so this models `Not` as logical negation of the preceding condition. Source: "// Transfer the conditions on the copy rhs, after inversing polarity." and "let conds = conditions.map(self.arena, Condition::inv);".
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically, the polarity inversion was applied for every `UnOp::Not`, including non-`bool` operands. Thus a condition equivalent to `(!a) == b` could be rewritten as the negation of `a == b`, i.e. `a != b`. The PR states: "jumpthreading was optimizing `!a == b` into `a != b` for non-bool, where this is definitely not true." The fix rejects the transfer for non-bool: "if !place.ty(self.body, self.tcx).ty.is_bool() {". The test comment records the same regression: "// Test for #131195, which was optimizing `!a == b` into `a != b`."
analysis.inputDomain: MIR containing a `Not` unary operation on a non-`bool` scalar, especially an integer wider than one bit (for example `i32`), whose result feeds an equality/inequality comparison or branch condition, processed by the JumpThreading MIR optimization. The added test uses `let mut a: i32 = 0; a = 1; if !a == 0 { 1 } else { 0 }`. Boolean operands remain valid for the polarity-inversion path. Both panic-abort and panic-unwind MIR test variants are included, while the semantic issue concerns the non-bool operand type rather than unwinding mode.
analysis.trigger: The `TOFinder` matches `Rvalue::UnaryOp(UnOp::Not, Operand::Move(place) | Operand::Copy(place))` and the operand type is not `bool`; before the fix it immediately inverted and inserted the known condition rather than returning.
preconditions: JumpThreading is running on MIR with a `UnOp::Not` copy/rhs pattern.
The `Not` operand place has a known condition that can be transferred.
The operand type is an integer or other non-`bool` type for which bitwise complement differs from logical negation.
pitfalls: Do not equate `Condition::inv` (branch polarity inversion) with computing the value of bitwise `Not`; they coincide only for `bool`.
`!a == b` parses as `(!a) == b`; for integers `!a` is the bitwise complement, not the logical negation of `a == b`.

The fix is intentionally conservative: the FIXME notes the case could be generalized only if the pass 'actually perform[s] a logical not on the condition's value', so simply allowing non-bool through is wrong.
The same MIR diff appears for panic-abort and panic-unwind; the correctness distinction is the operand type and condition transfer, not the unwind mode.
Do not conflate this issue with unrelated borrow or copied-place overwrite concerns; the patch's guard is specifically on the operand type.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a focused MIR-optimization test in `tests/mir-opt/jump_threading.rs` with a non-bool `Not`-then-equality condition, checking `CHECK-LABEL: fn bitwise_not(` and that the `switchInt(` remains. Emit the before/after MIR with `// EMIT_MIR jump_threading.bitwise_not.JumpThreading.diff` so the diff demonstrates the condition is not folded. Cover both `panic-abort` and `panic-unwind` MIR outputs. A separate runtime regression could compare `if !a == 0` against expected values for multiple `i32` values, but no execution or reproduction is claimed here because no compiler was built.
evidence: Fix #131195, where jumpthreading was optimizing `!a == b` into `a != b` for non-bool, where this is definitely not true.
